summary: Phase 4.1 of direct-route plan v2 landed: boxI_raise_step in Soundness.lean, the single-node interpretation-raise step of Simpson's Lifting Lemma 8.1.3 (chunks 0154-0155). Given a raw-edge-cond interpretation rho, a node x, and any w >= rho x, plus a designated raw-R-neighbour n of x (either direction), it produces rho' agreeing with rho off {x, n}, with rho' x = w, re-establishing the raw edge fact at the x-n edge (via cs5FCIncest_lift/F1 down, or cs5FCIncest_raise/F2 up) and Gamma-cond persistence at n via ckforces_persistence. Sorry-free and axiom-clean. Scoped build green, checkInitImports passes, no Preserved Asset regressed. Phase 4.2 (iterating this step over the finite tree to obtain the full boxI_lift and discharge the NIK.boxI case) is NOT attempted in this dispatch, per the single-phase (4.1-only) dispatch scope.

continuation_context.note: boxI_raise_step is deliberately scoped to ONE designated raw-R-neighbour n per invocation (not all of x's neighbours simultaneously), to keep the atomic step small and sidestep an unresolved bidirectional-edge case (R x n and R n x both holding for the same n, which the actual derivation-tree graph should never produce but which this lemma does not itself assume away). Phase 4.2 must invoke boxI_raise_step once per tree edge along a traversal outward from x (structural or well-founded recursion over the graph's finite construction via addEdge), chaining each newly-raised value forward to the next edge, to assemble the full Lifting Lemma boxI_lift. This is the plan's sole concentrated-risk phase; it carries its own hard budget cap and blocked-honesty exit to Phase 7, never an open-ended retry.

artifacts.summary: Added boxI_raise_step (lines 450-516), inserted between the Phase 2 TClosure section (dia_iff_TClosure) and the one-point soundness section. Statement: given cs5FCIncest r, upward-closure hyps v_uc/bf_uc for CKForces persistence, raw-edge-cond hedge : forall a b, R a b -> r (rho a) (rho b), x n : Label Atom with x <> n, w >= rho x, and hR : R x n or R n x, produces exists rho', rho' x = w and (forall z, rho z <= rho' z) and (r (rho' x) (rho' n) or r (rho' n) (rho' x)) and (CKForces at rho n implies CKForces at rho' n). Proved via classical (for the if-then-else Decidable instances), case-splitting on hR into the F1 (cs5FCIncest_lift) down case and F2 (cs5FCIncest_raise) up case, defining rho' as an explicit if-then-else re-interpretation at {x, n}.
Phase 4.1 heading updated to [COMPLETED]; both checklist items checked off with landed-location notes.

decisions_made: Scoped boxI_raise_step to ONE designated raw-R-neighbour n of x per invocation, rather than attempting to raise ALL of x's neighbours simultaneously in a single call. A single-invocation design covering arbitrarily many neighbours would need to resolve, for each neighbour z, whether R x z or R z x (or, pathologically, both) applies via a non-canonical Classical.choose per neighbour, and the both-directions-at-once case has no proof from cs5FCIncest alone without an additional antisymmetry-style hypothesis on R at x. Restricting to one neighbour per call keeps the lemma small, avoids that unresolved case, and matches the mission's 'Bounded unit: one lemma about a single raise' framing; Phase 4.2 is expected to invoke it once per tree edge.

Constructed rho' via an explicit `classical`-backed if-then-else function (not Function.update), because Function.update requires a `DecidableEq (Label Atom)` instance that is not available for a generic Atom; `classical` supplies the needed propositional Decidable instances for the if-then-else conditions z = x / z = n without imposing DecidableEq on Label Atom.
dead_ends: Function.update (Function.update rho n n') x w: fails to elaborate without a DecidableEq (Label Atom) instance, which is not derivable for a generic Atom type; also Function.update_noteq is not the correct Mathlib lemma name (it is Function.update_of_ne, with a different argument/direction convention) -- switched to an explicit if-then-else construction under `classical` instead.
